title: Chicken thigh, fried, coated, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Fried chicken thigh coated in a crispy breading. The skin and coating are not consumed, only the meat of the thigh. Served at restaurant (852) and is a popular source of protein and energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Deep‑frying creates a golden crust while keeping the interior juicy.
Chicken thighs contain more fat than breast meat, making them more flavorful when fried.
Traditional breading often combines flour, spices, and sometimes breadcrumbs.
In some cuisines the skin is removed before frying to reduce calories.
The dish is commonly served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, or garlic aioli.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The fat in the thigh offers sustained satiety and a quick energy source.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Proper cooking makes the proteins readily available for digestion.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Fried meat contains a notable amount of saturated fat, which may raise cholesterol levels if eaten frequently.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish is calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Trans fats in breading
items.content: If pre‑made breading mixes are used, they can contain trans fats.

items.title: Salt and spices
items.content: Excessive salt in the coating may be unsuitable for individuals with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume only the thigh meat, avoiding the skin and breading. Pair the dish with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, or whole‑grain products. To reduce calories, blot excess oil with a paper towel before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness. Do not keep at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
